title: Protocol for Immuno-Enrichment of FLAG-Tagged Protein Complexes
protocol: Transfect cells with the FLAG-tagged plasmid of choice.
Seed cells on 10 cm dishes to achieve 50% confluency 16 hours after seeding.
Prepare a microcentrifuge tube with 800 μL of Opti-MEM for each 10 cm plate.
Mix 8 μg of FLAG-tagged plasmid with 8 μL of Polymag.
Let the mixture sit for 20 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add DNA-Polymag complexes to cells.
Place 10 cm plate(s) on magnetic plate and let sit for 20 min.
Remove cells from magnetic plate.
Leave cells in incubator until ready for lysis (∼18–24 h).
Incubate 30 μL Sheep Anti-Mouse Dynabeads in each microcentrifuge tube.
Add 500 μl of IP Buffer/FLAG antibody master mix into each microcentrifuge tube containing Dynabeads.
Rotate the tubes end-over-end either at 4°C overnight (16–18 h) or for 2 hours at room temperature (20°-25°C).
Use screw cap microcentrifuge tubes with O-rings for immunoprecipitation.
Ensure optimal incubation of beads with the antibody using an end-over-end rotator.
Rotate gently to prevent bead fragmentation during incubation.
Avoid vortexing beads between steps.
Move plates directly from the incubator onto ice 18–24 hours after cell transfection.
Wash plates twice with 10 mL of PBS/Mg/Ca Buffer.
Tilt plate to gather excess PBS/Mg/Ca and aspirate carefully in the last wash.
Lose cells off each plate using a cell scraper into 300 μl Lysis Buffer.
Move lysate into a microcentrifuge tube and sonicate for 3 × 5 seconds.
Keep lysates on ice for 30 minutes.
Spin lysate at 16,100 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Move supernatant into new microcentrifuge tubes.
Measure protein concentration using BCA or Bradford assay.
Determine the total volume of lysate and add additional Lysis Buffer to bring final concentration to 1 mg/mL.
Keep 50 μL of each lysate for input and keep on ice.
Centrifuge tubes containing Dynabeads + FLAG antibody for 1 min at 16,100 × g at 4°C.
Place tubes on magnetic rack and aspirate off liquid using a gel loading tip.
Add 1 mL IP Buffer to each tube and rotate on end-over-end rotator for 5 min at 4°C.
Repeat steps of adding IP buffer, rotating, and centrifuging for subsequent washes as necessary.
Centrifuge tubes for 1 min at 16,100 × g after final wash and aspirate off liquid.
Add lysates to each prepared IP tube: For out-competition controls, add 490 μL of lysate in 10 μL of 3× FLAG Peptide (final concentration 340 μM) per tube.
For experimental conditions, add 500 μL of lysate at 1 mg/mL per tube.
Have an equal number of control and experimental tubes per experiment.
Let tubes containing lysate + beads rotate at 4°C for 2–4 hours on an end-over-end rotator.
Place tubes on a magnetic rack, and aspirate off the liquid using a gel loading tip.
Do one quick wash by adding 1 mL of IP Buffer to the tubes.
Turn the tubes up and down 10-15 times.
Centrifuge the tubes for 1 minute at 16,100 × g at 4°C and aspirate on the magnetic rack.
Add 1 mL of IP Buffer to each tube and put them on an end-over-end rotator at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge the tubes for 1 minute at maximum speed at 4°C and aspirate on the magnetic rack.
Repeat steps 29+30 four times.
Add 1 mL of IP Buffer into each tube and put them on an end-over-end rotator at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the tubes for 1 minute at maximum speed at 4°C and aspirate on the magnetic rack.
Prepare master mix of elution solution.
For each microcentrifuge tube, mix 16 μL of Lysis Buffer with 4 μL of 3× FLAG peptide to achieve a final concentration of 340 μM.
Add 20 μL of the prepared elution buffer to each microcentrifuge tube and place on ice for 2 hours.
Tap tubes approximately every 15 minutes during incubation.
Centrifuge tubes at maximum speed at 4°C for 1 minute.
Place tubes on magnetic rack.
Move elution solution/protein mixture into a new labeled tube.
If multiple tubes for the same condition, pool elutants into one microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1:1 μL of 4× Laemmli buffer to input tube(s).
Heat for 5 min at 75°C or 95°C.
Flash freeze elutants and heated input on dry ice.
Store at −80°C.
Concentrate eluants in order to run on a SDS-PAGE gel if proceeding with this step.
If skipping the concentration step, add 1:1 μL of 4× Laemmli buffer to elutants after heating for 5 min at 75°C.
Flash freeze and store at −80°C.
Measure volume of each individual sample.
Add 1.96 μL sodium deoxycholate per 100 μL of each sample.
Calculate TCA amount based on total volume after adding sodium deoxycholate and add to the mixture.
Incubate on ice for 20 minutes.
Centrifuge at 16,100 × g at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Carefully remove supernatant.
Add cold acetone in an amount equal to the volume of TCA added previously.
Centrifuge at 16,100 × g at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Carefully remove supernatant.
Leave tube open with a Kimwipe over the top and air dry for 5 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add 10 μL of 4× Laemmli buffer to the dried pellet.
If solution turns yellow, add 10 μL of 1 M Tris at pH 9.0 to neutralize the color.
Add another 10 μL of 4× Laemmli buffer if necessary.
Boil for 5 minutes at 75°C.
Load inputs and concentrated samples on an SDS-PAGE gel in duplicate.
Analyze one set of gels by protein stain (Silver stain or Coassive).
Confirm the amount of protein immunoprecipitated is sufficient for Mass Spectrometry analysis.
Transfer the second gel to a PVDF membrane.
Conduct immunoblot analysis using the FLAG antibody on the PVDF membrane.
Perform Western blotting to confirm enrichment of FLAG-tagged protein and effective out-competition with 3× FLAG Peptide.
Carry out silver staining to demonstrate sufficient enrichment of FLAG-protein complexes and identification of nonspecific binding proteins in the 3× FLAG Peptide control.
Use Mass Spectrometry to identify and exclude nonspecific binding proteins from the interactome of the protein of interest.
Submit eluted immunopurified complexes for Mass Spectrometry analysis.
Perform label-free or isobaric tagging approaches to identify hits from background.
Analyze peptides enriched two-fold compared to negative control using DAVID Analysis.
Categorize the interactome based on gene ontology.
